title: Concurrent short-path ranker orchestration to reduce tail latency
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: The current reranking endpoint exhibits long-tail latency for mixed-length queries and high-concurrency bursts. Root causes include monolithic microbatching that stalls short queries behind large token requests, late KV-cache warmup for cold requests, and conservative timeouts that cause head-of-line blocking. Goal: Reduce 95th/99th percentile latency for rerank calls by applying short-path scheduling, token-aware micro-sharding, and deadline-driven timeboxing while preserving top-K quality and throughput. Deliver a rolloutable feature flag with observability and safe fallback to existing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for rerank endpoint decreases by >=25% on production-like load compared to baseline
99th percentile latency improves by >=20% without decreasing normalized top-K NDCG by more than 1% in offline evals
No customer-visible error-rate increase; graceful degradation (partial scores) documented and tested
Feature gated behind rollout flag; can be disabled per-customer/route
Dashboards show per-lane latency, microbatch sizes, KV cache hit-rate, and early-exit frequency
implementation_notes: Introduce 'short-path' scheduling lane: route requests with token_count <= 64 and timeout < 300ms into a low-latency microqueue that prioritizes fast dispatch over aggregation
Token-aware micro-sharding: split long requests into bounded token-slices with independent timeboxes to avoid head-of-line blocking; assemble partial scores and re-rank at collector
Speculative parallelism: allow 2x speculative microbatches for short-path lane (configurable per-customer) to absorb burstiness; add early cancellation when top-K stability is detected

Deadline-driven timeboxing: attach per-request deadline budget propagated from API layer; enforce soft/preemptive timeouts at scheduler and hard timeouts at worker with controlled partial-return semantics
KV cache warmup: prefetch candidate embeddings for top-N candidates when re-ranking is signaled by a warm-start token pattern; backoff strategy if prefetch thrashes
Backpressure and throttling: integrate with existing token-bucket rate limiter; short-path lane can have separate burst buckets to protect throughput
Compatibility: maintain identical API semantics — partial results flagged with 'partial_score': true and 'reason' for early-exit; clients can request 'guaranteed_full' to opt-out
Configuration: expose per-organization knobs in console (short_path_enabled, short_path_max_tokens, speculative_factor, timebox_ms) with safe defaults
Observability: emit per-request tags: lane, microbatch_size, deadline_ms, early_exit, kv_prefetch_hit
Fallback: on overload, route to an 'approximate' ranker variant (quantized model) automatically with documented quality delta
testing_plan: Unit tests for scheduler decisions: lane assignment boundary cases, timebox expiry paths, speculative cancellation
Load tests in staging with realistic token-length mix (templates stored in tests/fixtures/rerank-length-distribution.json)
A/B experiment: 10% traffic ramp, monitor latency, error-rate, downstream client complaints for 48h before 50%
Offline quality eval: run on standard rerank prompt set (NDCG@10) comparing baseline vs short-path with partial returns included
Chaos test: simulate KV cache cold starts and network delays to validate graceful degradation
End-to-end test with SDK: ensure partial return plumbing and client opt-out works across Python/Node SDKs
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): feature flag on in dev + integration tests (complete)
Phase 1 (staging): enable for non-critical customer routes, validate metrics and reduce thresholds
Phase 2 (canary): 10% production traffic for low-volume orgs, monitor SLOs 72h
Phase 3 (ramp): 50% then 100% with auto-fallback to baseline if error-rate or quality regressions exceed thresholds
Rollback plan: disable feature flag and wait for in-flight requests to drain; clear speculative queues
risks: Quality regression from partial returns if collector assembly misorders partial scores
Prefetch thrash causing KV cache eviction and overall worse performance for other lanes
Complexity in tracing/observability leading to blind spots during incidents
Per-customer config combinatorics may create surprising interactions with Dedicated capacity limits
